title: Exact sensitivity certificates for planar transport maps: coefficient uncertainty, a convergent box refinement and a sharp three-atom calibration

claims.statement: Finite affine maxima define the unique quadratic optimal map to their own pushforward laws, almost everywhere under a uniform polygon source.
Rational cell overlays compute exact squared map discrepancy; a separate exact primal-dual witness certifies target transport cost.
claims.contribution: known constructions implemented as exact certificate infrastructure

claims.statement: The integrated possible-winner envelope bounds squared map error uniformly over every single global realization of the stated independent coefficient box.
claims.contribution: scoped certificate method: a transport-specific integration of established possible-winner (envelope) screening; historical priority not established
claims.qualification: Conservative for two distinct reasons (winner-slope incompatibility and pointwise parameter independence); no general relative-tightness guarantee (P6). Gap linear in the largest radius with an explicit constant (P7). Rational planar implementation, uniform source; not fixed prescribed masses.

claims.statement: On the strict admissible cube family F=H(s,b)+(a+s)b^2 and W2^2=|s|+(a+s)b^2, giving the exact overlap-coupling excess.
claims.contribution: elementary two-parameter extension of the credited OpenAI three-atom construction

claims.statement: For a fixed a and an admissible closed parameter rectangle, the exact maximum of F is attained at a corner; the symmetric-tilt pointwise envelope exceeds the sharp maximum by B/2.
claims.contribution: sharp specialized calibration and uncertainty-gap identity; priority not established

claims.statement: Adverse family on K=[1,2]x[0,1]: F(u,v_b) is the stated piecewise function of b, sup F = epsilon^2/4 at the interior parameter b=1-epsilon/2 with F=0 at both box endpoints, while the envelope and the slope-diameter baseline equal 4 for every epsilon in [0,1]; the compatibility-respecting pointwise supremum integrates to epsilon^2/2.
claims.contribution: exact diagnostic separating the two relaxations of P3; the family was supplied by the external review of version 0.1.0 and is rederived here
claims.qualification: A limitation of informativeness, not a counterexample to P3.

claims.statement: Tightness: 0 <= B - F(u,v_nominal) <= 2 r Lambda + 2 r^2 + 4 r R_K D_K n(n-1) Lambda/|K| with the stated rational constants; consequently any finite sub-box cover yields LB <= sup F <= UB with UB - LB <= gamma_box(r_*), and best-first bisection with feasible-realisation lower bounds converges with linear rate in the sub-box radius.
claims.contribution: new scoped theorem and implementation (refine_bound, tightness_bound); historical priority not established
claims.qualification: Uniform refinement needs a number of sub-boxes exponential in the box dimension 3n; the returned interval is valid at every budget.

assurance.externalReviewSuppliedByPublisher: version 0.1.0; major revisions; all items actioned (REVIEW_RESPONSE.md); authorship not recorded
assurance.crossVendorAdversarialReview: version 0.2.0 new results (P6, P7, refine_bound); see STATUS.md

limitations: Uniform source on rational convex planar polygon for the generic implementation
Own pushforward targets, not a prescribed-mass solver
Potentially expensive line arrangements; fail-closed region cap
No general sharp global-box maximum in closed form; the refinement is exponential in the box dimension
No downstream application or performance claim; the benchmark is a single-machine observation
